mainTopic: Wine and a גוי's touch: bringing grapes, the אתרוג in the barrel, payment for wine a גוי deliberately made forbidden, and a גוי plugging a leaking barrel
overview: This amud opens by finishing a debate between רב כהנא and רב יימר about letting a גוי bring grapes to the winepress. A ברייתא permits grapes a גוי brought, but רב כהנא answers that he was talking about לכתחילה, not after the fact. Next, an אתרוג falls into a barrel of wine. רב אשי tells the people to hold the גוי's hand still so he doesn't stir the wine, and to pour the wine off. רב אשי then rules that if a גוי deliberately makes a Jew's wine into יין נסך, the wine may not be sold, but the Jew may collect its value from that גוי, as if the גוי had burned it. He proves this from a ברייתא: he follows the תנא קמא that the wine is forbidden, and draws on the idea that the גוי acted against the owner's will. Finally, a גוי plugs a leaking barrel with his hand, and רב פפא rules that the wine next to the opening is forbidden. His ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: grapes in small barrels are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a ברייתא that רב יימר quoted against רב כהנא: grapes a גוי brings in small barrels are permitted, even if juice sprays onto them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And grapes brought in small barrels, even though the wine sprays onto them, are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: We are coming in at the end of a ברייתא that רב יימר quoted to challenge רב כהנא. It says grapes a גוי brought in small barrels are permitted, even though juice squeezed out and splashed on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא had said a גוי should not be allowed to bring grapes to the winepress, because juice comes out and he could make it forbidden. The ברייתא seems to say the grapes are fine even when juice sprays on them. So the ברייתא looks like it disagrees with רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Small barrels or containers used to carry grapes
Sprays or splashes
Permitted

phrases.english: and in small barrels,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַיַּיִן מְזַלֵּף עֲלֵיהֶן
phrases.english: even though the wine sprays onto them
phrases.notes: "Wine" here means the juice that squeezes out of the grapes as they get squashed on the way.

phrases.english: it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדוּדוֹרִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַיַּיִן מְזַלֵּף עֲלֵיהֶן — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began before this section, used as a challenge to רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that a גוי should not be allowed to bring grapes to the winepress.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits grapes a גוי brought, even with juice spraying on them, so there seems to be no reason to stop him from bringing them.

steps.title: רב כהנא answers: I was talking about לכתחילה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the ברייתא is about grapes that were already brought, while he was talking about what to do from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you talking about a case where the גוי already 'brought' them? I am talking about what we allow from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב יימר's challenge. The ברייתא says 'brought', which means after the fact, but he was talking about whether to let the גוי do it in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between בדיעבד (after it already happened) and לכתחילה (from the outset). The ברייתא only says that once the grapes arrived, they are not forbidden. That does not mean we should let a גוי bring them to begin with, so the two statements do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought (already happened)
From the outset; before doing the action
After the fact; once it already happened

steps.whatToRemember: A rule saying something is permitted after it happened (בדיעבד) does not mean we allow it from the outset (לכתחילה).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב כהנא is saying the grapes become forbidden. He agrees they are permitted once brought; he only says we shouldn't arrange it that way from the start.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא answering רב יימר.

phrases.english: Are you saying "brought"?
I am speaking about from the outset!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow a גוי to bring grapes, against רב כהנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about grapes already brought; רב כהנא's warning is about not letting the גוי bring them in the first place.

steps.title: The אתרוג that fell into a barrel of wine
steps.stepSummary: An אתרוג fell into wine and a גוי jumped to take it out; רב אשי told the people to hold his hand still and tip the barrel until the wine drained out.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אתרוג once fell into a barrel of wine, and a גוי jumped up to take it out. רב אשי told them: Hold his hand so he doesn't stir the wine, and tip the barrel until the wine drains out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about an אתרוג that fell into wine. רב אשי gives a practical way to keep the גוי from making the wine forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גוי's touch is unintended (he was reaching for the אתרוג), and such a touch without moving the wine does not make it forbidden, but stirring it does. So רב אשי has them hold the גוי's hand still, so it is only touching and not moving. Then they pour the wine off until it is gone from around his hand, and he can take the אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: An אתרוג (citron)
A barrel of wine
To stir or swish around
And tip it over so it pours out

phrases.english: There was a certain etrog that fell into a barrel of wine,
a gentile jumped up and went to take it.
Rav Ashi said to them:
Hold his hand still
so that he does not stir it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the wine. Stirring the wine is what would make it forbidden.

phrases.english: and tip it until it drains out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the related topic of a גוי touching wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a גוי's hand is in the wine, hold his hand still so he does not stir it, and pour the wine off; this way the wine stays permitted.

steps.title: A Jew may collect payment from a גוי who deliberately made his wine יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules: if a גוי deliberately makes a Jew's wine into יין נסך, the Jew can't sell it, but he can collect its value from that גוי, because the גוי basically burned it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If a גוי deliberately poured a Jew's wine as an idol offering, even though the Jew may not sell it to another גוי, he may collect its value from that גוי. Why? Because the גוי is like someone who burned it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new ruling. The wine itself is forbidden to benefit from, but the Jew can make the גוי pay for the damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling the wine would be getting benefit from יין נסך, which is forbidden. Taking money from the גוי who ruined it is different: it is payment for damage, like making someone pay for wine he set on fire. The payment is for the loss, not for the wine itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Poured it as an offering to an idol
On purpose; deliberately
To collect its value (its price)
He burned it; he destroyed it completely

steps.confusionAlert: Taking money from the גוי is not 'selling' the forbidden wine. It is payment for damage he caused.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows an important idea: a person who makes someone's property forbidden can be treated like someone who destroyed it, and must pay.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי גּוֹי דְּנַסְּכֵיהּ לְחַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכַוָּונָה,
phrases.english: This gentile who intentionally poured a Jew's wine as a libation,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְזַבּוֹנֵיהּ לְגוֹי אַחֲרִינָא אָסוּר,
phrases.english: even though it is prohibited to sell it to another gentile,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְמִישְׁקַל דְּמֵיהּ מֵהָהוּא גּוֹי.
phrases.english: he is permitted to collect its value from that gentile.
What is the reason?
He burned it completely.
phrases.notes: He didn't really burn it, but making it forbidden ruined it just as much as burning it would.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַאי גּוֹי דְּנַסְּכֵיהּ לְחַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכַוָּונָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רב אשי about a גוי who deliberately ruins a Jew's wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may not sell wine a גוי deliberately made into יין נסך, but he may collect its value from that גוי as payment for damage.

steps.title: רב אשי brings his source: a ברייתא about a גוי who poured a Jew's wine
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks where he learns his ruling, and quotes a ברייתא: wine a גוי poured not in front of an idol is forbidden, but two תנאים permit it for two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Where do I learn this from? From a ברייתא: A גוי who poured a Jew's wine as an offering, but not in front of an idol, makes it forbidden. רבי יהודה בן בבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירא permit it for two reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts proving his ruling from step 4. He quotes a ברייתא where the תנא קמא forbids the wine and two תנאים permit it, and this step is setting up the two reasons that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, the גוי poured the wine as an offering but not in front of an actual idol. The תנא קמא says the wine is still forbidden. רבי יהודה בן בבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירא disagree and are about to give two reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introducing a source)
Not in front of an idol
They permit

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi says: From where do I say this?
As it is taught in a baraita:
A gentile who poured a Jew's wine as a libation
not in front of an idol, it is prohibited,
but Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava
and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira permit it
for two reasons:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי begins bringing a source for his ruling in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's ruling that the Jew may collect payment from the גוי who ruined his wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה בן בבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.title: The two reasons: no offering without an idol, and 'you can't forbid my wine against my will'
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons for permitting: people only pour wine to idols in front of an idol, and the Jew can say, 'You have no power to forbid my wine against my will.'
steps.simpleTranslation: First: people only pour wine as an offering in front of an idol. Second: the Jew can say to the גוי, 'It is not in your power to forbid my wine against my will.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the two reasons why רבי יהודה בן בבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירא permit the wine. The second reason is the part רב אשי uses for his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: an offering not in front of an idol isn't a real offering. Reason two: the גוי acted against the owner's will. רב אשי still follows the תנא קמא that the wine is forbidden, which is why it may not be sold (step 4); he borrows only the 'against my will' idea, which makes it damage the גוי must pay for.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not in your power
Against my will; by forcing me
They pour wine as an offering to an idol

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי follows the תנא קמא that such wine is forbidden. He uses the idea that the גוי acted against the owner's will to rule that the גוי must pay for the wine he ruined.

phrases.english: One: that they do not pour wine as a libation
except in front of an idol,
and one: that he says to him:
phrases.notes: The Jew, the owner of the wine, is talking to the גוי.

phrases.english: It is not in your power
to make my wine forbidden against my will.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד — שֶׁאֵין מְנַסְּכִין יַיִן אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two reasons announced at the end of step 5, completing the ברייתא רב אשי uses as proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's ruling that the Jew may collect payment from the גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: the תנא קמא forbids the wine, matching רב אשי's ban on selling it. The second reason ('It is not in your power to forbid my wine against my will') shows the גוי acts against the owner's will, which supports making him pay.

steps.title: A gentile plugs a leaking barrel with his hand
steps.stepSummary: A barrel's stopper came out and a גוי plugged the hole with his hand. רב פפא rules that the wine next to the opening is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a barrel of wine whose stopper came out. A גוי came, jumped up, and put his hand over the hole. רב פפא said: all the wine that is right next to the opening is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story and gives רב פפא's ruling on it. The ruling is not finished yet; it continues on the next amud to explain what happens to the rest of the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי touched the wine directly with his hand, and wine a גוי touches is forbidden. רב פפא limits the problem to the wine right at the opening, where the hand actually touched it. This sets up what the rest of the ruling says about the rest of the barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel or large jug for wine
The stopper or tap-hole of a barrel
Was removed, came out
Jumped up, leapt
Next to, facing
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not forbid the whole barrel here. He only talks about the wine next to the opening that the hand touched.

phrases.english: There was a certain barrel of wine
whose stopper had been removed,
a gentile came, jumped up,
and placed his hand on it.
phrases.notes: He put his hand over the hole to stop the leak, so his hand touched the wine.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
All the wine that is next to the opening is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case story about a גוי touching wine, after the earlier discussion of רב אשי's ruling and its proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a גוי plugs a barrel's opening with his hand, the wine next to the opening, which he touched, is forbidden.
